I went to look at my plants earlier because I realized during this past week, even though I've been watering them, I've been neglecting to take a close look at them. I decided to start weeding my tomato crate, because it's getting out of control, and that's when I noticed that there's mushrooms growing in the crate.

I don't know anything about mushrooms, so I was wondering if you guys could help me out... What kind are they, are they edible, should I even be concerned? How do I get rid of them, do I just pull them out?

Here's three pictures from the crate, each of different mushrooms growing.

Sorry, I have no idea how this happened or how to prevent it in the future, this is my first year and I'm just trying my best with what little knowledge I learned through research during the winter months...

Mushrooms are a good thing. Healthy soil includes fungi. The mushroom is only the flower, so even if you pulled them out, the fungus is still living below the soil surface. Mushrooms help decompose woody material so you could take it as a sign that your rich, healthy soil is being used up and losing its structure, and that you should add mulch or compost next year to maintain its health.

Those look a bit like liberty caps, a type of magic mushroom.
Thanks, that's good to know! I feel a lot better now! :D

DO NOT EAT!!! Very few fungi are edible. Most are not. The few that are edible are almost always easily confused with poisonous fungi. Expert level knowledge is the only way to not get yourself hurt or killed. If you want to eat wild fungi, find an expert and learn everything you can for a few years. Otherwise, it's best to avoid eating wild fungi.
